encounters.cc: Progressive hand weakness, difficulty walking, and occasional slurred speech

lines: Progressive hand weakness, difficulty walking, and occasional slurred speech

The patient is a 59-year-old male with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, obstructive sleep apnea with poor CPAP adherence, prior upper gastrointestinal bleeding, and polycythemia vera previously managed in Hematology, who presents to the Neurology clinic with a 6-month history of progressive weakness in his hands and difficulty walking.
He reports that he frequently trips over his own feet and has difficulty holding onto objects, which has led to him dropping cups and utensils.
He also mentions occasional slurring of his speech, especially when tired.
His past medical history is significant for hypertension.
- Esophagogastroduodenoscopy with variceal band ligation (prior admission)
On examination, you note atrophy of the intrinsic hand muscles and fasciculations in the upper extremities.
His gait is spastic, and he has hyperreflexia in the lower extremities with an upgoing Babinski sign.
Routine blood work, including complete blood count, electrolytes, renal function, and liver enzymes, is within normal limits.
An EMG shows widespread denervation with both acute and chronic changes in multiple myotomes.

lines: Progressive exertional dyspnea, leg swelling, and mild abdominal discomfort

lines: Sudden-onset hematemesis with fatigue and abdominal swelling

- Esophagogastroduodenoscopy with variceal band ligation (prior admission)
